bug_semantics: Authenticated CWE-434 RCE via POST /admin/tinymce/upload (admin.tinymce.upload). TinyMCEController::storeMedia() accepted any uploaded file, stored it on Laravel's default public disk under tinymce/, and returned Storage::url() so the file was web-reachable. No MIME/extension allowlist existed. At introduction the sink was $file->store('tinymce') (Laravel hashName/guessExtension); libmagic reports a PHP one-liner as text/x-php, so a crafted .php payload was persisted as a public .php object. On 2.2.x (including PoC commit ba25b7e7) the same sink used getClientOriginalExtension() plus storeAs, so the client-supplied .php suffix was kept even if Content-Type was spoofed as image/jpeg. Bouncer exempts this route from ACL, so any logged-in staff user can upload a webshell and execute it with a GET to /storage/tinymce/<file>.php.
flaw_origin: The unrestricted public TinyMCE upload handler was first written on 2024-07-23 in 64b90d623f8a03c602392baaa5f880ea5377eaf6 ('email template page.') by suraj kashyap while adding packages/Webkul/Admin/src/Http/Controllers/TinyMCEController.php and Route::post('tinymce/upload', ...). The parent tree had the TinyMCE Blade client (including a dangling route('admin.tinymce.upload') reference from f1314ae74) but no controller, no tinymce/upload route, and no storeMedia. 47a9c723b later refactored store() to storeAs + getClientOriginalExtension() during SVG sanitization; that aggravated client-extension control but did not first create the sink. The 2.2.x attack path is the same handler behind user middleware.

reasoning: CVE-2026-38526 is a real published MITRE record (not withdrawn/rejected). The mechanism is unrestricted TinyMCE media upload to a public, executable path. The smallest first-write of that sink is 64b90d623f8a03c602392baaa5f880ea5377eaf6, which created TinyMCEController::storeMedia() with unvalidated $file->store('tinymce') and Storage::url(). Immediate parent 201b7e569 lacks the controller and the tinymce/upload route (verified with cat-file and git grep), so introducer_parent_absent is true. PR #1292 is a two-commit merge, not a squash; 64b90d623 is already the member that first wrote the lines, so squash_decomposed is false. 47a9c723b is not the BIC: it only rewrote an existing public-store sink to trust getClientOriginalExtension(). The 2.2.x PoC (ba25b7e7) still executes that same handler. Auth on 2.2.x is the user middleware wrapping Admin routes; ACL is skipped for this endpoint. The patch that closed the sink is 082e3df27 (allowlist + content-derived extension); it landed via merge 6e37f391 / PR #2585 and is first tagged in v2.2.4, which is after the affected 2.2.0–2.2.3 window.
